520	The same relationship between spirituality and physicality, between the desert and the Land of Israel, exists also
521	in the Torah as a whole, between Torah and mitzvot. The spies wanted to stay in the desert. What did they want?
522	To learn Torah or to fulfill mitzvot? To learn
523	Torah. After all, in the desert it is impossible to fulfill
524	most of the mitzvot, because most of the mitzvot depend on the Land,
525	whereas entering the Land is what allows us to fulfill
526	the mitzvot. But when one is occupied with fulfilling mitzvot, is it
527	possible to be less occupied with Torah? And the proof, notice
528	a simple fact:
529	All the Torah we have in our hands today, we have the five
530	books of the Torah. But when someone wants to learn Torah, his
531	main occupation in Torah is with the Talmud, the Mishnah,
532	and the Talmud.
533	But do we have any Torah from the period of the entry
534	into the Land? The people of Israel entered the Land through Yehoshua,
535	and were there 850 years.
536	They went out to exile for 70 years and returned afterward to the
537	Second
538	Temple, and only at the end of the Second Temple did the period of the Tannaim
539	and the Zugot begin, and they began, in essence, to invest
540	in Torah, and from them we have the Mishnah and the Talmud.
541	Before that, they did not learn Torah? Certainly they learned Torah, but
542	they learned Torah in a much more spiritual way.
543	Why? Because generally the people were busy with
544	physical and earthly work, with working the land. They were not
545	free to occupy themselves with Torah and its wisdom as later
546	the Tannaim
547	and the teachers did.
548	Wait, Yehuda HaNasi later gathered all that
549	they had said orally. Yes, yes. But our point is
550	that he gathered what the Tannaim said orally, which is a
551	completely different period. Certainly, yes, that is the Mishnah, he gathered
552	the Mishnah. But in any
553	case, we see that the emphasis upon entering the Land is
554	not on occupation with Torah. Again, not that they did not occupy themselves,
555	certainly they did occupy themselves with Torah, and the tribe of Yissachar was always occupied with Torah;
556	that was its role. But in general, among the people as a whole,
557	the main emphasis was on fulfilling the mitzvot, and fulfilling
558	the mitzvot is the emphasis of drawing the light down, the Infinite
